sentinel_preservation_proof.method: planted a pre-existing sentinel body in each owned child, ran the mode, compared SHA-256 and mtime_ns
sentinel_preservation_proof.fix_note: install_sentinel previously rewrote the sentinel every run, so sentinel_stable compared a fresh file against itself and reported false. Now the prior bytes+mtime are captured before the run and restored afterwards.

originals_verification.method: resolve_original() per sample: binding + SHA-256 recomputed from disk, cross-checked against gold and the ROOT sample_manifest.json
originals_verification.note: mtime_ns values were identical before and after every read; no original was copied or written.

honest_counterfinding.finding: cn-ir recall failure is not a cap problem
honest_counterfinding.detail: cn-ir had only 11 candidates and the selector selected all 11, yet 9 of 10 gold facts remain absent. The candidate generator never produced those facts, so raising the selection cap cannot fix cn-ir recall.

bugs_found_and_fixed_this_session: recovery.peak_rss_bytes() returned None on Windows: ctypes called GetProcessMemoryInfo without argtypes/restype, so the 64-bit HANDLE was truncated and both psapi and K32 probes returned 0. Added prototypes; peak RSS is now really measured (12.2 MiB native, 21.0 MiB offline).

install_sentinel() unconditionally overwrote an existing sentinel, and the sentinel_stable check then compared that fresh file against itself, so it could never detect a clobbered pre-existing sentinel. Now the prior bytes+mtime are captured before the run and restored byte-identical afterwards; restoration.sentinel_restored reports 'restored' vs 'created_by_this_run'.
restore_sentinel() had a NameError typo ('preeexisting') that the new sentinel-preservation test caught before it shipped.
config_unchanged reported count=0 when no --probe-config was passed, which could look like a pass while proving nothing; the probe count is now printed and the sentinel is included in the probe set.
